import crypto from "crypto";

const TOLERANCE_SECONDS = 300;

export function verifyWebhook(rawBody: Buffer, header: string, secret: string): boolean {
  const parts = Object.fromEntries(header.split(",").map(p => p.split("=")));
  const t = parts["t"];
  const sig = parts["v1"];
  if (!sig) return false;

  if (t) {
    const age = Math.abs(Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) - Number(t));
    if (age > TOLERANCE_SECONDS) return false;
  }

  const expected = crypto
    .createHmac("sha256", secret)
    .update(`${t ?? ""}.`)
    .update(rawBody)
    .digest("hex");

  return expected === sig;
}

verify.ts only applies the 300s age check if `t` is present. The HMAC covers `${t ?? ""}.` + body, so a sender that signs with `t=` cannot have it stripped without breaking the signature. The exposure is limited to senders that ever sign without `t=`. Confirm whether Tallyport ever does this.

handler.ts takes the key from `req.body.event_id` after signature verification. acquireKey (SET NX EX 86400) is atomic and runs before chargeCustomer. verify.ts compares `expected === sig`. Timing leak is theoretical here given the HMAC construction. Recommend crypto.timingSafeEqual.

### F4 (Reliability): key is consumed even if charge fails
If chargeCustomer throws after acquireKey succeeds, the event is marked processed for 24h and the charge is never retried. Not a security issue but can lose payments.

### F5 (Informational): no amount validation in charge.ts
Marked TODO. Amount comes from a signed payload, so exploitation requires the secret.
